proof_summary: Positivity supplies prime witnesses that, according to parity, directly give Goldbach and Lemoine representations above the stated thresholds, while direct finite computation handles all smaller required cases. For infinitude, every sufficiently large even \(n\) is written as \((p-6)+q+6\), with both \((p-6,p)\) and \((q,q+6)\) cousin-prime pairs; finitely many such pairs would yield only finitely many possible \(n\), contradicting the infinitude of large even integers.
